newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices rise, seen tracking Germany.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices rise, seen tracking Germany.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose in early Monday trade and dealers expected them to shadow German paper in the absence of any local indicators before Wednesday's wholesale prices.
"It doesn't look as if Denmark will do anything independently today. We expected thin turnover," a trader said.

At 0745 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 111.94, yielding 6.18 percent, up from Friday's 111.88. The seven percent 2007, due to become the benchmark on September 1, was up to 104.63, with a yield of 6.37 percent, from 104.45 on Friday.
The 2006 bond's yield gap to the 10-year bund was 45 basis points, compared to Friday's 46. The 2007 was 65 basis points over the bund, unchanged from Friday.
The crown was also unchanged, at 3.8080 to the mark.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 fell 0.10 point, to 90.05. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
